pl-l2d19c5-d1e108.summary: Asks whether, if there had been no command to eat of the tree of life and he ate of others, man could have avoided death.

pl-l2d19c5-d1e111.summary: Reasons that if he would live always without that tree, his ability not to die was not from it; if not, it was from it.

pl-l2d19c5-d1e114.summary: Reports some who say that without the command he would have lived always eating other trees, reading Augustine's 'from the tree of life, not the condition of nature' as 'not from nature only, but also from the tree.'
claims: One view: immortality came partly from nature.

pl-l2d19c5-d1e118.summary: Reports others who think the ability not to die came from the tree of life, not nature: he could not die because he could use the tree, eating of which he would not die.
claims: Another view: immortality came wholly from the tree of life.

pl-l2d19c5.summary: Asks whether, had there been no command to eat of the tree of life and he ate of others but not it, man could have not died. Some say he would have lived always, reading Augustine's 'from the tree of life, not from nature' as 'not from nature only.' Others say the ability not to die came from the tree of life, not nature: he is said able not to die because he could use the tree.
claims: One view: man could have lived without the tree of life; immortality was not from nature only.
Another view: the ability not to die came from the tree of life, not nature.
